correctness.rationale: For P_s strong K_(1,m), s>=2,m>=3, the strong-product distance is max(path gap,star gap). The standard auxiliary graph linking selected vertices when path gap exceeds star gap has no odd cycle by the chord/sign-alternation argument, so is bipartite; each independent part injects into a GP set of the star of size at most m. A 2m-set forces each part to project onto the unique m-leaf maximum GP set; no centers, each leaf selected exactly twice. Analyze any triple in distinct occupied path layers: two nonadjacent gaps forbid all leaf assignments; a single gap=1 forces disjoint labels in the adjacent pair; both gaps=1 prohibit only threefold repetition, impossible under twice-per-leaf. Five layers force an obstructed triple, and 4-layer sets consist of two disjoint consecutive pairs. Counting support cases gives C(s,2)+(3^m-3)(s-2)+(2^m-2)(s-2)(s-3)+(2^m-2)^2 C(s-2,2). An independent BFS/geodesic brute force for representative (s,m) and leaf-position enumeration confirmed all four cases, with all arbitrary-parameter content supplied by the analytic structural argument. The known scalar gp=2m is credited to Vesel, not newly proved.
